newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sketch of Algeria's new constitution.
newsitem.headline: Sketch of Algeria's new constitution.

text.p: Here are the main points of Algeria's new constitution which the government said on Friday was overwhelming endorsed in a national referendum held on Thursday.
It replaces the 1989 constitution, which ended the sole ruling party era. It broadens the president's paramount powers but limits him to two five-year terms.
It also sets up a second parliamentary assembly, named the Council of the Nation, whose speaker may succeed temporarily the president in the event of his death or impeachment.
The text guarantees for the first since 1962 independence of the North African oil and gas producing country's 28.3 people the right to form opposition parties to compete for power.
But it bans politicians from using Islam, Arab and Berber languages, gender and regional differences as weapons to gain power.
The draft displays the authorities' concern over budget deficit by preventing parliament from proposing any law which results in burdening the state financial balances.
Following are selected quotes from the draft:
* Algeria, land of Islam (and) part and parcel of the Great Maghreb, is an Arab, Mediterranean and African country...
* The state draws its legitimacy and raison d'etre from the people. Its motto is "By the people and for the people".
* The elected assembly is the framework in which the people express their will and control of the authorities' action.
* The public propriety belongs to the national community. It comprises subsoil, minerals and quarries, natural energy sources, mining and national sea resources...

* The right to create political parties is recognised and guaranteed....the political parties are not allowed to be founded on religious, linguistic, race, gender, corporatist and regionalistic basis.
* The law sanctions the duty of parents to ensure protection and education for their children as well as the duty of children to help and assist their parents.
* The family benefits from the protection of the state...
* All citizens have the right to a job. The right for protection, security and health in the workplace is guaranteed.
The draft empowers the president to name prime ministers, to appoint to senior jobs the heads of councils set up to oversee administration and Islamic affairs.
* The president should be of original Algerian nationality and of Moslem faith, being aged more than 40 years the day of his election and should prove his wife is an Algerian national.

* The president should prove his parents were not involved in actions hostile to the November 1954 Revolution if he was born after July 1942. He should prove that he took part in the November 1954 Revolution if born before July 1942.
The Algerian parliament is made up of the National Assembly and the Council of the Nation.

* National Assembly deputies are elected in universal, direct and secret suffrage. Two-thirds of the members of the Council of the Nation are elected in indirect and secret votes by local assemblies. The last one-third of the members of the Council of the Nation are picked by the president among national personalities and competencies in scientific, cultural, professional, economic and social fields.
